shared_turn_1.assistant_response:
We don’t usually feel pain while asleep because sleep changes how the brain processes sensory signals. The thalamus and sensory cortex become less responsive, attention is reduced, and the brain’s natural pain-modulating systems are more active. But pain isn’t truly switched off. Strong or threatening pain can still reach the brain and wake you. In fact, poor sleep can make you more sensitive to pain afterward.
